meta.title: Sort import:  Uncoditionally removes JSX Fragment reference
meta.fix_ref: microsoft/TypeScript#41441 (fix(41194): ignore jsxFrag identifier in import declarations), 03877260f8, 2020-11-24; git tag --contains: first in v4.2-beta / v4.2.2
meta.build_notes: npm typescript@4.1.6 (the last 4.1 release; the fix is not on the 4.1 branch) and typescript@4.2.2 (2021-02-25), both behind typescript-language-server@0.7.1, started with the pinned tsserver.js; the reported TypeScript version is checked on every session. Deviation from the wrapper rule: the release current at 4.2.2 (0.5.1) offers no organize-imports code action (attempt 1: only 'Move to a new file' for the whole-file range); 0.7.1 offers source.organizeImports, followed through its _typescript.organizeImports command.
meta.notes: The report names VS Code's 'Sort Imports' (organize imports without removing unused imports, added later); the wrapper of the era exposes 'Organize Imports' (source.organizeImports), which runs the same unused-import analysis that drops frag. Removing frag leaves the fragment factory named by /** @jsxFrag frag */ unresolved. Invalid after two attempts, both case-spec errors: the edit spec carried no code-action kind, so the request had no context.only and the wrappers (0.5.1 and 0.7.1) returned only 'Move to a new file'; source actions such as organize imports are returned only when requested with only: ['source.organizeImports']. The bug itself was never exercised.

settings_note: The issue names no compiler options besides the pragmas in the file; no tsconfig.json, so tsserver uses an inferred project (the wrapper's inferred options enable JSX).

files.source: issue body, first tsx code block
files.note: the file name is not given in the issue; 'lib' is not installed, which does not matter for the import analysis

repro.steps: Open index.tsx (a JSX file with /** @jsx h */ and /** @jsxFrag frag */ pragmas importing h and frag). Run the source action that organizes imports. Reported: frag is removed from the import although the fragment <>...</> uses it (a runtime error follows); expected: frag stays. Probe: after the edit, a fresh session on the edited file must not report an error the case session did not report before (the targeted diagnostic is an unused-import report, which organize imports is meant to clear).

attempts.summary: Builds 4.1.6/4.2.2 behind the era wrapper 0.5.1: the whole-file code-action request offered only 'Move to a new file'; that wrapper exposes no organize-imports code action, so the probe could not be evaluated (invalid on both builds).
